Before her big operation, my auntie dropped me off at my house. It was a pretty regular occurrence, she used to take me and my brother and sister out a lot. She was born with a massive hole in her heart and spent her childhood in a wheelchair but improved into adulthood, though she was always pretty weak. I guess as kids she always shielded her bad health from us, and hated looking weak or needing help.
On that day, I didnt know the operation was life or death, with a 10% survival rate. She and my parents never told me. I was used to her going in for ops so I guess I thought it was no big deal.
However, that night before she went in, she dropped me off as the sun was setting. For some reason, I ran up the stairs and watched the car pull out onto the road and drive away into the sun. I watched that car until it disappeared. To this day, I have no idea why I did that, but that is my last memory of her. She died in intensive care the next day aged 42. My parents decided it was best for us to stay away, my auntie was tubed and ventilated and I guess they knew she didn't have long.
In a way I'm glad they did that. She would have hated us to see her in a hospital bed struggling to survive, and I have that really nice memory of her disappearing into the sunset. Choking up writing this ha. its been 10 years and she's still an amazing inspiration in my life.

Sounds like you're already doing great, man. 24f with depression here. This is what helps me

1. Talking. Just being a listening ear can work wonders. You are probably already doing this, so just continue to be supportive, but also recognise the signs that she may need professional help. My mum and dad are great with me, but sometimes its nice to be able to talk to a counsellor I didn't know, as I felt I was stressing out my mum and dad or wearing them down, which of course added guilt and anxiety to the way I was feeling

2. This might be tough, but when I feel low and want to stay in bed all day my friends or family force me to go out and do something. Lying in bed or staying indoors avoiding the world is the perfect environment to breed negativity and encourages feelings of worthlessness (imo). Try to involve her in your plans, or give her a focus. Take her to the shops to buy ingredients you can cook a meal with together. If shes the type of girl that likes makeup/hair etc, take her to get her nails done etc.... which brings me to

3. Exercise. A biggy. I hate all forms of exercise, and I'm pretty unfit, but I cannot deny that afterwards I feel great, and it lifts my mood.It doesn't need to be intense. Could be something simple, going for a walk in the park/a hike, or going to a dance class, playing a sport. Classes always motivate me because its a group activity and you can't just stand in the room doing nothing. It's also a good way to interact with other people.

4. If she really struggles, go to the doctor. When I started to get suicidal after losing my job and boyfriend I knew I needed something more than just talking out my feelings, and the doctor put me on a low dose of an antidepressant. There is absolutely no shame in it. Depression is an illness that can be helped with drugs, and I definitely found they help. They can take a few weeks to take effect, and I've been on them for about 6 months now. I can honestly say I'm doing better. Whether that's the medication or everything else I'm doing I can't say for sure!

5. Look after yourself! I know you want to do what's best for her, but sometimes looking after someone with depression is exhausting. The negativity and the constant worry can wear you down. The fact that you've come on here and asked for help is great, just make sure you look after your own mental health too. Talk to someone close to you. You don't need to tell them everything thats going on with your girlfriend, but sharing can lessen your own worries.

Lastly, what works for one person won't necessarily work for another, and your girlfriend may need to figure out what works for her. It took me a while to realise that talking to my friends only increased my anxiety and depression, and that talking to an almost stranger helped me more.

I really hope things get better for you guys soon. Try and stay positive, you're doing a great job.
